{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABi7ymRw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhMSCn0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 411, "title": "Remove implicit provisional TEXT filtering from desktop focused text output", "body": "## Problem

The desktop Focused Application Text Output node accepts the generic `TEXT` contract but silently discards deliveries marked provisional. The user clarified that this violates the graph/node design: the graph wiring, not an implicit policy in the sink, determines which text is sent to the focused field.

At current main [922ecc9](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/commit/922ecc9d90c769e013f0fd6b04a9876d9c1dcb56), [desktop/focused-output.js](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/922ecc9d90c769e013f0fd6b04a9876d9c1dcb56/desktop/focused-output.js#L11-L14) includes `!context.provisional` in its delivery condition. A valid nonempty TEXT routed explicitly to the sink is therefore ignored solely because of its upstream delivery metadata. [The extension's corresponding sink](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/922ecc9d90c769e013f0fd6b04a9876d9c1dcb56/extension/page-output-node.js#L35-L49) does not impose this filter. Existing desktop tests and documentation explicitly encode the unwanted policy.

## Expected outcome

- Remove the provisional filter from the desktop focused text sink. Each valid nonempty TEXT delivery during its active authorized lifecycle follows the same existing insertion path, regardless of provisional/committed metadata, source node identity, port name or producer type. Do not introduce an equivalent filter elsewhere in the host, queue or runtime.
- Keep the default desktop graph wired to ASR `final`, so ordinary default dictation continues to insert only final results. A user who explicitly connects `provisional` (or another compatible TEXT-producing route) instead gets the text actually delivered by that route. The sink must not decide which ASR result the user wanted. No implicit rewriting of saved graphs.
- The sink remains ordinary append/insert, using existing native input semantics. It does not implicitly replace earlier provisional text, merge provisional/final values, deduplicate equal deliveries, or acquire hidden history. Replacing provisional text with final text is a separate feature/design discussion and explicitly out of scope for this Issue.
- Preserve lifecycle authorization: the existing active-session signal check, cancellation/cleanup rejection, Stop drain, stale callback rejection, and normal native target/clipboard handling remain unchanged. Empty strings remain insertion no-ops; this change is not a request to interpret an empty string as deletion.
- Do not change the semantics of shared ASR or processor nodes (including TextFormatter's existing preview handling) merely to force a particular upstream output. The sink forwards whatever TEXT those nodes actually emit along the selected wire. Do not modify the browser extension unless a directly equivalent hidden filter is found in its focused-output path; the inspected extension sink already accepts provisional metadata. No new port, setting, feature flag, mode, abstraction, or unrelated refactoring.
- Update the desktop node help and guide, and any misleading comments or test names, to distinguish the generic sink's behavior from the default final-only wiring.

### Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] A deterministic Pipeline test connects a generic TEXT producer (or its provisional port) directly to the focused sink and demonstrates that provisional and final deliveries are both forwarded in order, including repeated equal text. A final-only wiring test demonstrates that unconnected provisional output is not inserted. Preserve existing cancellation and stale-signal regressions.
- [ ] Adjust the existing tests in `tests/desktop.test.js` and `tests/desktop/macos.test.js` that expect the sink to discard provisional deliveries, according to the new contract. For routes through a formatter, assert the actual output of that processor is forwarded, rather than changing the formatter's own established behavior. Keep tests representative.
- [ ] Run `npm test`, applicable affected desktop tests/build checks and `git diff --check` using the lightest appropriate layer. This is a small node-policy fix; no exhaustive native-app matrix, new real-model run, or permission-dependent human verification is required. Report unrun optional checks accurately. Do not revisit the focus/clipboard edge cases already scoped in #407 and #409.
- [ ] Confirm that the default graph still selects final output and that existing graph schema, browser/extension behavior, and desktop insertion mechanisms remain unchanged. Update documentation and PR description.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Context

Follow-up to #401, #407 and #409. The repository's [node design principles](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/README.md#design-principles), [port contracts](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/port-contracts.md) and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md#node-architecture) require producer-independent contracts and explicit graph composition rather than hidden producer/preview policy in a generic sink. Follow [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md).
